newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tellabs Oct calls out, stock up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tellabs Oct calls out, stock up.

text.p: Investors were selling October positions in Tellabs Inc options and taking longer-dated positions as as the shares rallied on Wednesday.
By 1105 CDT (1605 GMT), Tellabs was up 5-3/4 at 78-3/4 on more than 3.2 million shares. The stock reached an intraday high of 80-1/4 in early trade.

"There are a lot of option sellers in October closing out positions," said John Oppenheimer at Oppenheimer, Noonan & Associates at the Pacific Stock Exchange. He said the activity was coming from institutions including Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers as well as retail investors.
In the November and December calls, investors were doing a lot of covered writing, Oppenheimer added.
The most active Tellabs option was the December 75 call, which traded about 2,900 contracts. Its open interest was just over 3,000. The option was up 2-5/8 at 8-1/2.
The October 80 call traded about 1,600 contracts, the October 75 traded about 1,150 and the October 70 call traded around 500.
The most active put was the October 75, which traded 760 contracts and fell 2-3/8 to 1-1/8. Its open interest was 58.
Oppenheimer said volatility in the Tellabs options had dropped about 10 percent.
Marty Kearney at PTI Securities in Chicago said the options' average volatility was around 48-1/2 but the October 75 calls had dropped to about 43.
He said the October puts were trading with volatility in the mid-40 area, but in November and December, where put volume was small, volatilities were holding steady.
Arakis Energy Corp, the Canadian energy company with options listed on the CBOE, continued to see heavy public buying and selling of the October five calls.
The stock, which trades on the Nasdaq stock market, was down 13/32 at 3-3/4 after declining to 3-14/32 in early trade.
The shares declined after the company said had not yet reached an agreement with any potential partner on its Sudan Petroleum project.

On Tuesday, the stock rallied after the company confirmed it was in active negotiations with parties from various countries to form a consortium for development associated with the Sudan Petroleum project.
The stock closed at 4-5/32 on Tuesday and options with expirations in November, January and April were added.
On the CBOE, the October five call traded about 3,775 contracts. Its open interest, including an addition of 950 on Tuesday, was a heavy 25,135.
"It's just a continuation of yesterday," said the designated primary market maker at the CBOE. "The public's on both sides."
He said that while few of the newly-listed options had traded, he expected activity in those options to pick up.
The November five call traded 300 contracts, the April five call traded 183 and the January five call traded 100.
--Gregory Crawford, (312) 408-8750
